description:
FILED s398 (Fable, #153 FOLD chunk 3 review probes; occurs in NO population as a failing row — filler).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main (13bcef4) and on the chunk-3 branch; the term walker / fold are not involved (the arrow spelling `(qw(a b), {q=>7})[2]->{q}` is empty too).

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratchpad probes/qw2.pl, qwh.pl):
    print (qw(a b), "c")[2]        perl: c      PCL: (empty)   SILENT WRONG
    print (qw(a b), "c")[0]        perl: a      PCL: ab        SILENT WRONG (the qw list is ONE element)
    my @l = (qw(a b), "c"); $l[2]  perl: c      PCL: c         (assignment flattens correctly)
    print ((qw(a b)), "c")[2]      perl: c      PCL: (empty)
    print ("a","b","c")[2]        both: c
    print (qw(a b), {q=>7})[2]->{q} perl: 7      PCL: (empty)

CAUSE (to confirm): the list-slice reduction (legacy CtorSub — `<tree_val>` + Constructor, list_ctx_subscript metadata) sees the parenthesised list's tree_val whose qw child is a single QuoteLike::Words node; the a_ref_acc/list-slice lowering indexes the tree_val's CHILDREN positionally instead of the FLATTENED list, so a multi-word qw counts as one element (index 0 = the whole qw as a string "ab", index 2 = nothing).  Assignment (`@l = (...)`) flattens through p-flatten-args, which is why it is right.

FIX SHAPE: the list-slice lowering must flatten the sliced list the way list assignment does (one mechanism — reuse the flattener), never index the tree_val children.  Guard rows in Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t (probe vs perl first): the shapes above + INVERSE `(1,2,3)[1]`, `(f())[0]`, `qw(a b c)[1]` (works: the QW branch), `(@a, @b)[1]` (arrays flatten too — probe perl).  BAR: corpus-diff (list-slice files may change: ref.t/grep.t — each diff explained), gate, sweep.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a qw() INSIDE a sliced parenthesised list — `(qw(a b), "c")[2]` is empty and `[0]` yields "ab" (the qw is not flattened under the slice)
